title: CSS stylesheet review
when: The user wants a stylesheet reviewed for maintainability, responsiveness, accessible styling and dead or conflicting rules.
prompt:
Goal: A CSS review flagging specificity trouble, fixed sizes, missing states and unused rules, each with the selector and a fix.
Steps:
1. Check braces and parse by eye; every rule after a missing brace is broken.
2. Specificity: ids in selectors, chains deeper than three, more than three !important, overrides fighting each other; suggest single class selectors.
3. Responsiveness: widths over 400 px, px heights on text boxes, no media query or fluid grid, overflow at 320 px.
4. Accessible styling: outline removed without a :focus-visible replacement, fonts under 12 px, failing color pairs, motion without prefers-reduced-motion.
5. Consistency: raw values that should be tokens, duplicate declarations, prefixes no longer needed.
6. Dead code: search each class in the HTML and list selectors that match nothing.
Quality bar:
- Every finding quotes the selector.
- Fixes keep the look unless the finding is a bug.
- Severity marked.
Pitfalls:
- Demanding a naming methodology the project never used.
- Missing a rule that never applies because of source order.
- Approving outline: none.
Verify:
- [ ] Specificity hot spots listed.
- [ ] Fixed widths and tiny fonts listed.
- [ ] Focus and motion rules checked.
- [ ] Unused selectors checked against the HTML.
Output: review.md with findings under Responsive, Accessibility, Maintainability and Dead code.

examples.input: meu CSS esta uma bagunca, revisa pra mim
examples.output: 7 !important, #header .nav ul li a chains, width 960px wrapper, 12 unused selectors, outline none on buttons
